recipes.name: Beef Rice Noodles
ingredients: 200 g / 7oz rump steak / top sirloin (, cut into 3 - 4mm / 1/8" slices, or other steak - see Note 1)
1/2 tsp baking soda ((bi-carbonate) - NOT baking powder, won't work)
2 tbsp peanut oil (, canola or other neutral flavoured oil)
200g / 7 oz Pad Thai-thickness flat rice noodles (~3-4mm (1/8" wide), or any other - see Note 3 for quantities)
3 garlic cloves (, finely minced with a knife)
6 - 8 baby bok choy, choi sum stems, Chinese broccoli
1 tbsp light soy sauce (, or all-purpose soy or tamari for gluten-free (Note 2))
3 tbsp oyster sauce ((can substitute with vegetarian oyster sauce))
Pinch white pepper ((or black pepper, or chilli flakes))
instructions: Tenderise beef - toss with baking soda, leave 20 min, rinse, season with soy sauce. Stir fry - Sauté onion first, then beef, then garlic, then stems. Add leafy greens, prepared noodles, and sauce. Toss well then serve.
Tenderise - Sprinkle the beef with baking soda in a small bowl. Toss with your fingertips to coat, separating the beef slices. Leave for 20 minutes to tenderise.

Rinse, dry, season - Rinse in a colander, shake and pat off excess water with a paper towel (no need to be thorough). Place in a bowl and toss with the soy sauce. Set aside. (It doesn't need marinating time).
Sauce - Mix ingredients in a small bowl.

Soak and rinse noodles - Prepare the noodles according to packet directions (usually soaking in boiling water for 5 - 10 minutes). Drain, then rinse under tap water to remove excess starch so it doesn't go gluey when cooked.

Cook onion, beef then garlic - Heat the oil over high heat in a large wok or large deep fry pan / skillet (~30cm/12"). Add the onion for 30 seconds. Add beef and cook until the red is almost gone (~1 minute), then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

Stems then everything else - Add the stem part of the Asian greens, toss for 1 minute. Add the leafy part, noodles then sauce (in that order). Toss for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes until the sauce has stained all the noodles and there is no sauce left in the base of the pan. Serve immediately!

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Beef cuts – Rump steak (US: Top Sirloin is my go-to beef cut for stir fries, for taste and value. I like to buy a roast (better value), portion and freeze. Porterhouse (strip) and scotch steak (rib eye) are also terrific but pricier. Other options: Top side (US: top round) – I get a roast and portion, flank. Slow cooking cuts – like chuck, oyster blade, gravy beef – use a slightly heaped 1/2 teaspoon and leave for 35 min, rinse. proceed with recipe. Blade and bolar need 40 min, the only cut I don’t use is brisket (just doesn’t seem to tenderise). Chicken or pork option – Use 250g/8oz boneless chickens thighs or any pork chop (a little more because the sauce is one I made with beef in mind which has a stronger flavour). If using breast, also use 250g/8oz and tenderise it using the same directions and baking soda amount as the beef in this recipe. 2. Soy sauce substitutes: – Light soy sauce can be substituted with all-purpose soy or tamari (for GF). Do not substitute with dark soy sauce, it’s way too intense. – Dark soy can be substituted with light soy, all-purpose soy or tamari though the noodles won’t be stained the brown colour you see. 3. Rice noodles – I use the Pad Thai thickness flat rice noodles which are ~3 – 4m / 1/6″ wide when dry. For other dried rice noodles, use the following quantities and increase beef to 250g/8oz (because you get more noodle volume): Extra wide ~1cm/0.4″ ( Pad See Ew thickness) – 250g/8oz Vermicelli rice noodles ~1mm – 175g / 6oz 4. Leafy Asian Greens – You can really use any here, just make sure thicker stems are cut lengthways so they are all roughly the same thickness so they cook through in around the same time. You could even use English spinach, or chopped cabbage (5 – 6 cups, chopped into bite size pieces). 5. Scaling up – To double the recipe, you’ll need to cook in a slightly different order else the pan the pan gets too crowded. Use a large 30cm/12″ pan. Follow the recipe as is, but when you add the stems, also add 2 1/2 tbsp of the sauce, then after 1 minute of cooking, tip everything out of the pan into a bowl. Add a bit more oil then add the leafy party of the greens, noodles and sauce, toss until the sauce reduces and you no longer see it in the base of the pan. Add the beef etc back in, toss through, serve immediately. Tripling – I would do as above for doubling the recipe, but then for the second part of the cooking (ie leafy veg, noodles and sauce), do that in two batches else your pan will be VERY full and difficult to toss. It’ll only take a few minutes per batch. Leftovers will keep for 3 days in the fridge. Not suitable for freezing (noodle breakage on reheat). Nutrition per serving for 2 generous portions.
